markdown.headingText: Generate a program to create charts using only R Graphics or ggplot2 or any R packages.
markdown.markdown: #### Variable Width Column Chart ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='hide'} library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # Data data <- data.frame( category = c("Company A", "Company B", "Company C", "Company D", "Company E"), value = c(10, 20, 15, 30, 25), width = c(2, 3, 1, 4, 2) ) # Calculate cumulative positions for x-axis data <- data %>% mutate( xmin = cumsum(lag(width, default = 0)), xmax = xmin + width ) # Update plot titles and labels for Market Share Analysis ggplot(data) + geom_rect(aes( xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = value, fill = category )) + geom_text(aes( x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, # Center of each bar y = value, label = paste0("$", value, "M") ), vjust = -0.5, size = 4) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") + labs( title = "Market Share and Revenue Analysis", x = "Companies", y = "Revenue (in Millions)" ) + theme_minimal() + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") + theme( text = element_text(family = "serif"), # Apply serif font to all text plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), # Title font size and style plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, face = "italic"), # Subtitle customization axis.title = element_text(size = 12), # Axis title font size axis.text = element_text(size = 10), # Axis tick labels font size legend.text = element_text(size = 10) # Legend font size ) ``` #### Table or Table with Embedded Charts ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} library(tidyverse) library(gt) # Sample Data product_data <- data.frame( Product = c("A", "B", "C"), Total_Sales = c(500000, 300000, 700000), Monthly_Sales = I(list( c(50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100), c(30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80), c(70, 90, 110, 130, 150, 170, 70, 90, 110, 130, 150, 170) )) ) # Function to create and save charts create_and_save_mini_chart <- function(monthly_sales, product_name) { chart <- ggplot(data.frame(Month = 1:12, Sales = monthly_sales), aes(x = Month, y = Sales)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + theme_void() + theme( plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank() ) file_name <- paste0("charts/chart_", product_name, ".png") ggsave(file_name, plot = chart, width = 4, height = 2, dpi = 150) return(file_name) } # Generate and save charts product_data <- product_data %>% rowwise() %>% mutate( Mini_Chart = create_and_save_mini_chart(Monthly_Sales, Product) ) # Create a table with embedded absolute image paths product_data %>% select(Product, Total_Sales, Mini_Chart) %>% gt() %>% fmt_currency(columns = "Total_Sales", currency = "USD") %>% text_transform( locations = cells_body(columns = "Mini_Chart"), fn = function(x) { paste0("") } ) %>% cols_label( Product = "Product", Total_Sales = "Total Sales", Mini_Chart = "Monthly Sales Chart" ) %>% tab_header( title = "Sales Performance by Product", subtitle = "Visualized with Embedded Charts" ) %>% opt_all_caps() %>% opt_table_font(font = list(google_font("Roboto"))) ``` #### Bar Chart ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load necessary library library(ggplot2) # Create example dataset: Average test scores by subject education_data <- data.frame( Subject = c("Math", "Science", "History", "English", "Art"), Average_Score = c(85, 90, 78, 88, 70) ) # Create and display the horizontal bar chart ggplot(education_data, aes(y = reorder(Subject, Average_Score), x = Average_Score, fill = Subject)) + geom_col() + labs( title = "Average Test Scores Across Subjects", x = "Scores", y = "Subjects" ) + theme_minimal() + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") + geom_text(aes(label = Average_Score), hjust = -0.2, size = 4, family="serif") + theme( text = element_text(family = "serif"), # Apply serif font to all text plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), # Title font style axis.title = element_text(size = 12), # Axis title font size axis.text = element_text(size = 10), # Axis tick labels font size legend.text = element_text(size = 10) # Legend font size ) ``` #### Column Chart ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load necessary library library(ggplot2) # Create example dataset: Government annual budget allocations in millions government_data <- data.frame( Sector = c("Healthcare", "Education", "Defense", "Infrastructure", "Public Services"), Budget_Million = c(70, 40, 60, 50, 30) ) # Create and display the column chart (vertical bars) ggplot(government_data, aes(x = reorder(Sector, Budget_Million), y = Budget_Million, fill = Sector)) + geom_col() + labs( title = "Annual Budget Allocations by Government Sector", x = "Sectors", y = "Budget (in Millions)" ) + theme_minimal() + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") + geom_text(aes(label = Budget_Million), vjust = -0.3, size = 4) ```
